consent_notice: Project X uses your own voice recordings to train an AI singing voice model, certify your voice profile, and create songs you request. You must be 18 or older and signed in to your own account. Choose one required retention option below. Development use is optional and does not extend retention. After local transfer is verified, audio is deleted from Render's active storage. Snapshot and backup copies may remain for an unknown period; active-storage deletion does not confirm removal of all copies. Read the full consent document before starting. Short Key Finder voice previews may be temporarily hosted on Render and are deleted from active storage after the final key choice or when the session ends; snapshot copies may remain. Pressing Finish and Start Training approves the saved Sections 1–8 takes for training. Section 9 is excluded from training.

consent_choices.delete_after_order: I agree to record my own voice and use it for AI voice-model training, certification, and my current song order. I choose deletion of my recordings and voice profile from active storage within 3 calendar days after this order is complete. This deadline does not apply to snapshots or backups; their permanent deletion timing is not confirmed.
consent_choices.future_purchases: I agree to record my own voice and use it for AI voice-model training, certification, and my current song order. I choose to keep my recordings and voice profile for my future song purchases until I withdraw permission or request deletion.
consent_choices.development_use: Optional: I allow my recordings and voice profile to be used for internal product development and testing while retained under my chosen option. This does not extend retention or authorize public release, and it does not affect my current song order.

sections.title: Sustained vowels
sections.instructions:
Ah — Eh — Ee — Oh — Oo

Hold each sound for about 2 seconds, taking a natural breath between sounds.

Follow this sequence

Middle: Sing all five sounds once on a comfortable middle note.

Lower: Move slightly lower and sing all five again.

Give your higher voice some attention.

To help us capture more of your singing range, make a clear effort to reach the higher notes you can sing comfortably. Explore above your usual speaking range and give those notes a little extra practice.

A lighter voice is fine. Aim for a clear, steady sound without shouting or squeezing. If a note feels strained, come down slightly and try again.

Higher: Choose a comfortable higher note and sing all five sounds twice at that same pitch.

Finish: Hold Ah, then Oh, in your comfortable higher range. Let any natural vibrato happen without forcing it.

Allow approximately two minutes, including your breaths. Take your time and follow the example at a comfortable pace.

Choose notes that feel comfortable for your voice. Keep the sound relaxed and steady, and avoid straining for high notes.

sections.title: Smooth scales
sections.instructions:
Sing a five-note pattern going up and coming back down

123454321

Sing the pattern using each sound

Ahahahahahahahahah

Eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

Ohohohohohohohohoh

Naynaynaynaynaynaynaynaynay

Take a natural breath between lines. Keep a steady, comfortable pace and connect the notes smoothly.

Complete four passes

Middle: Sing all four lines in a comfortable middle range.

Higher: Move into your comfortable higher register and repeat all four lines.

Higher again: Repeat all four lines at that same higher pitch.

Lower: Move into a comfortable lower range and repeat all four lines.

Give the higher passes your attention. Explore above your usual speaking range with a clear, relaxed sound. If you feel strain, come down slightly and try again.

Allow approximately two minutes overall, including natural breaths between lines. Follow the example at a comfortable pace.

sections.title: Arpeggios and pitch jumps
sections.instructions:
1. Sing the wider pattern

Low → Middle → High → Highest → High → Middle → Low

Sing this pattern once using each sound:

Ahahahahahahah

Heyheyheyheyheyheyhey

Mummummummummummummum

“Highest” means the top note of this pattern, within your comfortable range.

2. Make clear pitch jumps

Move directly between the low and high notes:

Low AH→High AH→Low AH

Low EE→High EE→Low EE

Low OH→High OH→Low OH

Low HEY→High HEY→Low HEY

Make a clear difference between your low and high notes. Give your higher register a chance to be heard, using a lighter voice if that feels natural.

Keep your throat relaxed. If a jump feels strained, bring the high note down slightly.

Take natural breaths and work steadily through the patterns. Aim for approximately one minute.

sections.title: Singing passage
sections.instructions:
Sing these twelve lines

Follow a gentle, steady, sing-song melody. Keep the same rhythm for each line, with a natural breath between phrases.

Baby, bring the sunshine to me.

Take the road and tell me your name.

Golden skies shine bright through the rain.

Sweet summer winds blow through the trees.

Charlie chased the shadows at night.

Every memory stays with me.

Sing it softly, sing strong and clear.

Hold me close and never let go.

Walking down the road in moonlight.

Bright blue morning, burning so bright.

Whisper every word and sing true.

I can hear you calling me, too.

Now try a different melody

Repeat these final four lines with a different tune:

Walking down the road in moonlight.

Bright blue morning, burning so bright.

Whisper every word and sing true.

I can hear you calling me, too.

Follow the example at a comfortable pace, with a natural breath between phrases. Allow approximately two minutes overall.

There’s no need to invent a complicated tune. Focus on sounding like yourself, with clear words and relaxed singing.

sections.title: Different ways to sing
sections.instructions:
1. Change your delivery

Sing this line seven times:

“I can hear the river calling my name.”

Softly — gentle, clear and audible.

Normally — your everyday, comfortable singing voice.

Strongly — a confident, comfortably fuller sound.

Softly with natural vibrato — allow any natural wavering in your voice.

Strongly with natural vibrato — keep the fuller sound comfortable and relaxed.

Smooth and connected — let the words flow together.

Short and rhythmic — give the words a light, bouncy rhythm.

Natural vibrato is welcome when it happens. You don’t need to force or manufacture it.

2. Change your range

Sing this line three times:

“Stay with me tonight.”

Once in your lower range.

Once in your normal range.

Once in your comfortable higher register.

Give the higher version a clear, deliberate try. Keep it relaxed, using a lighter voice if that feels natural.

Take a breath between versions. Let each one sound clearly different, and aim for approximately 1 minute 40 seconds overall.

sections.title: Clear words at a quicker pace
sections.instructions:
Sing these four lines

Running down the highway with the radio playing,

Everybody’s talking but I don’t hear what they’re saying.

Turn another corner, see the morning light,

We’re gonna keep on moving through the middle of the night.

Now change it up

Sing all four lines again using a different melody or rhythm.

Keep your voice relaxed and your words clear. If a line trips you up, slow it down, practise it, then try again at a comfortable pace.

Clear words matter more than speed.

Aim for approximately 25 seconds for each pass. Use a little extra time to repeat any difficult line—approximately 1 minute 10 seconds overall.

sections.title: Short notes and clear starts
sections.instructions:
1. Sing the short phrases

Ba — ba — ba — ba — baby

Pa — pa — pa — pa — paper

Da — da — da — da — daylight

Ta — ta — ta — ta — take me

Ga — ga — ga — ga — going

Ka — ka — ka — ka — carry

Fa — fa — fa — fa — falling

Va — va — va — va — valley

Give each repeated syllable a short note, then sing the final word or words naturally.

2. Change the vowel sounds

Meemaymahmohmoo

Neenaynahnohnoo

Leelaylahlohloo

Keep each sound distinct while maintaining an easy rhythm.

Use clear, natural pronunciation without exaggerating the sounds. Take a comfortable breath between lines and allow approximately 1 minute 20 seconds overall.

sections.title: Sing like yourself
sections.instructions:
Move through four parts

Your verse voice
Sing comfortably, as you would in a quieter part of a song.

Your chorus voice
Use a stronger, fuller sound while staying relaxed.

Your higher singing voice
Give your comfortable upper register some extra time. Explore those higher notes clearly, using a lighter voice where it feels natural. Come down slightly if you feel strain.

Your own finishing touch
Sing whatever makes you sound most recognizably like yourself.

Choose your words

Improvise your own words or use these original Project X lines:

I’ve been walking through the changes,

I’ve been waiting for the sun.

Each road holds a memory,

Every ending had begun.

So carry me home through the darkness,

Carry me home through the storm.

You can repeat the lines and vary the melody as you move through the four parts.

Follow the example at your own pace and allow approximately 2 minutes 15 seconds overall. Focus on a natural performance that sounds like you.

finish_standard.title: Finish Standard
finish_standard.text: Save at least one take in each of Sections 1–8. A natural performance with useful range, clear words and comfortable singing matters more than perfection. Feel free to repeat any section for better results.
